The body-rate setpoint genuinely is out of ANGLE_MAX scope in firmware (input_rate_bf_roll_pitch_yaw integrates the rate into the attitude target unbounded), so a contract tester checking the documented command-clamp contract legitimately sees 0 violations -- this is the real C2 seam, not a checker that was hobbled. provenance.concerns: No provenance fault found; the documentation sources are real and the policies are faithful, not strawman-weakened. (2) FS_EKF_THRESH was absent from the sample param snapshot (returned None); per ekf_check.cpp:42 if g.fs_ekf_thresh<=0 the EKF failsafe is disabled entirely, which would also explain T1c never firing -- I could not confirm the SITL default was >0 from the snapshot, but this does not weaken T1c (a disabled-and-thus-silent EKF failsafe is consistent with the documented contract; T1c only claims a configured limit is not spuriously actuated). (3) The XKF4.FS exclusion is defensible on contract grounds, but it is also the single most plausible signal that COULD discriminate OverDraw dynamics from the EKF side; the authors are honest that this is a 'leakage trap,' and the source confirms FS is a raw internal flag distinct from the failsafe actuation -- so excluding it is correct, but reviewers will scrutinize it. (4) T1c's predicate is actuation-only (ERR/MODE events); it cannot detect a limit that SHOULD have been configured but was not -- but that is a scope question for the experiment design (P held fixed with fence disabled), not a faithfulness defect in the policy as stated.

leakage.explanation:
I tried hard to refute non-circularity and could not. No oracle-A consequence signal enters any Tier-1 policy by any route (direct field, proxy, or window/gating).

CODE-LEVEL (planc/src/contract_baseline_v1.py):
- File reads are restricted to inputs. load_run_from_csv (L249-271), load_run_from_bin (L309-365), and _params_snapshot (L235-246) open only *_parsed.csv, *_command_profile.json, *_params.json. The string "oracle.json" never appears in executable code; AST-stripped scan confirms opens_oracle=False. The only *.oracle.json read is in the DRIVER run_contract_baseline_v1.py:239 inside oracle_a_cross_reference(), a separated ground-truth block that consumes the ALREADY-COMPUTED r["tier2_any"] + label and never feeds check_run().
- Tier-1 evaluators (_eval_T1a L492, _eval_T1b L519, _eval_T1c L526, _eval_T1d L539, _failsafe_events L504) read only command_profile.roll_deg/pitch_deg, params.ANGLE_MAX/FENCE_ENABLE, ERR.subsystem_name/ecode, MODE.mode_name/reason_name, MSG.text(failsafe markers). A forbidden-token scan over the AST-stripped source of all five (run.pos, run.xkf1_vd, run.xkf4_fs, rel_home_alt, ATT roll/pitch, DesRoll/DesPitch, CRASH_CHECK, CRASH_FAILSAFE, ground markers, .window() ) returns CLEAN for every one.
- XKF4.FS (the named leakage trap) is APPENDED at ingest only (L209/296/356, all marked AUDIT ONLY) and READ by zero evaluators. CRASH_CHECK / CRASH_FAILSAFE are excluded from the Tier-1 PREVENTIVE sets (L96-114) and live only in the Tier-2 CRASH_DETECTOR sets.

GATING/WINDOW:
- run.window() (L216-229) is derived purely from INPUT timing: first GUIA |RollRt|/|PitchRt|>=5 deg/s onset (L288-289) plus operator command_profile duration + fixed OBSERVATION_AFTER_PROFILE_S=18s. GUIA is confirmed in ArduPilot source to be the operator-commanded attitude TARGET, not achieved state (Log.cpp:546-560 "Guided mode attitude target information"; mode_guided.cpp:626-652 logs ang_vel straight from the SET_ATTITUDE_TARGET command). window() is invoked ONLY by the three Tier-2 evaluators (L572,582,596); NO Tier-1 evaluator references it.
- The failsafe/mode scan is whole-run and NOT crash-gated: _failsafe_events / _eval_T1d iterate run.errs/run.modes/run.msgs with no time bound. Verified empirically — an injected BATTERY_FAILSAFE at t=99999 (far past any crash) is still detected.

BEHAVIORAL INVARIANCE (clean_unsafe run oracleAv1_grid_default_r0180...s01, which crashes at t=82.96s; Tier-1 baseline=[]): zeroing all achieved ATT.Roll/Pitch, dropping all POS/XKF1/XKF4, deleting all ground-contact MSGs, truncating the whole trace at crash time, and INJECTING fake SIM-Hit-ground + CRASH_CHECK ERR + CRASH_FAILSAFE mode at post-window time ALL leave Tier-1 unchanged at []. Conversely the detector is live (non-strawman): injecting a real FAILSAFE_BATT ERR flips T1b to hit, and PC_FENCE/PC_GCS/PC_CLAMP controls fire the expected Tier-1 policies.

Conclusion: Tier-1 is consequence-invariant at field, value, code, window, and behavioral levels. The non-circularity claim holds; C2 is not undermined by leakage.

No oracle-A consequence signal enters any Tier-1 policy, verified at the field, value, code, window/gating, and empirical levels in /mnt/nvme/px4_work/uav_sparse/planc/src/contract_baseline_v1.py.

(1) DIRECT FIELDS: Independent AST extraction of run.* attributes used by the executable bodies of _eval_T1a/b/c/d and _failsafe_events (lines 492-552) shows they touch ONLY run.command_profile, run.angle_max_deg, run.params, run.errs, run.modes, run.msgs. They never reference run.att (achieved Roll/Pitch), run.pos (RelHomeAlt), run.xkf1_vd (descent rate), or run.xkf4_fs (raw EKF bitmask). All four consequence channels are structurally absent from Tier-1. XKF4.FS is parsed into run.xkf4_fs (line 296) but referenced by NO evaluator (not even Tier-2) -- audit-only as documented.

(2) WINDOW / CRASH-TIME GATING: run.window() (lines 216-229) is called ONLY by the three Tier-2 evaluators (lines 572, 582, 596); monkeypatching window() to raise did not trip any Tier-1 evaluator. The window end = start + prof_dur + 18s is a fixed offset from INPUT timing, not crash time, and start derives from guia_active_t (rate-command active = input) or demanded-attitude onset, never achieved state. Empirically, truncating a crashing OverDraw run to before its first 'SIM Hit ground' left Tier-1 identical ([]) while Tier-2 dropped T2c -- Tier-1 is crash-time independent.

(3) VALUE-LEVEL LEAK THROUGH SHARED errs/modes/msgs CHANNELS: CRASH_CHECK is excluded from PREVENTIVE_FAILSAFE_SUBSYSTEMS and the T1c subsystem set by MEMBERSHIP (not via the ecode!=0 filter); CRASH_FAILSAFE is excluded from PREVENTIVE_MODE_REASONS and explicitly continue-skipped in T1d (lines 547-548, CRASH_DETECTOR_MODE_REASONS). Ground/crash STATUSTEXT matches no T1b PREVENTIVE_TEXT_MARKER, and no preventive marker contains crash/ground/hit -- no substring cross-contamination.

(4) T1d SAFETY_MODE BRANCH (the only theoretical consequence-leak path: a crash-induced autoland into a SAFETY_MODE with a non-excluded reason would fire T1d on a consequence): across all 607 OverDraw runs the ONLY mode transitions are GUIDED/GCS_COMMAND, STABILIZE/INITIALISED, GUIDED_NOGPS/GCS_COMMAND -- all operational. The vehicle crashes in GUIDED_NOGPS; the firmware never autolands, so this branch never fires. T1d=0 on all 607.

(5) SIDECAR: contract_baseline_v1.py never opens *.oracle.json in executable code (grep + AST confirm only comments/docstrings mention 'oracle'). The runner run_contract_baseline_v1.py reads the sidecar ONLY in oracle_a_cross_reference() (line 239), strictly downstream of check_run, comparing the already-computed tier2_any to the recorded label; the label never feeds back into any Tier-1 decision. Re-running anti_leakage_audit() against current source: field_set_disjoint=True, value_level_ok=True, code_level_ok=True (no forbidden tokens, opens_oracle_sidecar=False), passes=True.

Conclusion: the Tier-1 contract layer is consequence-clean. The C2 non-circularity claim holds.

No oracle-A consequence signal enters any Tier-1 policy, verified at field, value, code, call-graph, and real-data levels.

(1) NON-CIRCULARITY HOLDS. A transitive call-closure analysis of every Tier-1 evaluator (stronger than the checker's hardcoded 5-function token scan) shows none of them, through any reachable helper, touch the consequence attributes: _eval_T1a -> {_eval_T1a,_f}; _eval_T1b -> {_eval_T1b,_failsafe_events}; _eval_T1c/_eval_T1d -> themselves. None reads run.pos (RelHomeAlt), run.att (achieved Roll/Pitch), run.xkf1_vd, or run.xkf4_fs (the latter is explicitly labelled "AUDIT ONLY; not used by Tier-1" at contract_baseline_v1.py:209,296). T1a (:492-501) reads only command_profile + angle_max_deg, which are operator INPUT, not consequence.

(2) WINDOW/GATING IS CONSEQUENCE-INDEPENDENT AND TIER-1 NEVER CALLS IT. RunData.window() (:216-229) derives start from guia_active_t (input rate-command timing) and end from command-profile duration + fixed 18s; it never uses crash time, altitude, or achieved attitude. It is invoked only by _eval_T2a/b/c (:572,582,596). No Tier-1 evaluator references window().

(3) FAILSAFE/MODE SCAN IS NOT GATED ON CRASH TIME. _failsafe_events (:504-516), _eval_T1c (:526-536), _eval_T1d (:539-552) iterate the FULL run.errs/run.modes/run.msgs lists with no lo<=t<=hi bound and no crash-time reference (confirmed; a heuristic flag on _eval_T1d was a false positive from the substring "hit" inside a dict key).

(4) SHARED-FIELD VALUES ARE DISJOINT. T1b's only consequence-adjacent read (run.msgs) is filtered to PREVENTIVE_TEXT_MARKERS ('failsafe','ekf failsafe','thrust loss','deadreckon','fence breach'), which has ZERO substring overlap (both directions) with GROUND_CONTACT_TEXT ('sim hit ground','crash'). CRASH_CHECK / CRASH_FAILSAFE are excluded from PREVENTIVE_* sets (:113-114).

(5) REAL-TRACE CONFIRMATION. In the sample crashed-but-clean trace, the only consequence messages are 17 'SIM Hit ground' STATUSTEXTs (Tier-2 only); the lone ERR is COMPASS ecode 0 (all T1 require ecode!=0); MODE reasons are all INITIALISED/GCS_COMMAND (operational, excluded from T1d). Nothing consequence-derived can produce a Tier-1 hit.

(6) CHECKER NEVER OPENS THE ORACLE SIDECAR IN EXECUTABLE CODE. AST-stripped checker source has no 'oracle.json'/'.oracle' literal. The orchestrator run_contract_baseline_v1.py:229-257 reads *_parsed.oracle.json, but ONLY inside the separated oracle_a_cross_reference() ground-truth block for an agreement statistic; the label is never fed to check_run, any evaluator, or the Tier-1 path of decide() (which uses only tier1_any_hits).

MINOR NOTE (not a leak): THRUST_LOSS_CHECK is in PREVENTIVE_FAILSAFE_SUBSYSTEMS and 'thrust loss' is a text marker. ArduPilot crash_check.cpp:100 thrust_loss_check() is a documented PREVENTIVE guard distinct from post-impact crash-check, so its Tier-1 classification is defensible; if it fired it would INCREASE Tier-1 hits (refuting C2), not manufacture a false pass. It does not fire in the inspected trace. I re-ran the anti-leakage audit independently: passes=true, intersection=[]. I could not find any vector — direct field, proxy, helper, window, or sidecar — by which a consequence signal reaches Tier-1.

completeness.overall_assessment:
VERDICT: No genuine, documented FC (Tier-1) contract was found that both (a) is faithful to firmware/PGFUZZ semantics and (b) fires on the contract-clean OverDraw region. C2 survives the completeness attack, but with one important caveat the authors must pre-empt in print.

THE STRONGEST THREAT IS PRESENTATIONAL, NOT SUBSTANTIVE. A reviewer/competing checker can lift the ANGLE_MAX doc string ('maximum lean angle in ALL flight modes', ArduCopter/Parameters.cpp:350-357) into a policy on the DESIRED attitude (ATT.DesRoll/DesPitch) -- call it C-DESATT. Empirically it fires hard on the sample trace (max demanded lean 176.7 deg vs 45; sustained 22.2 s) AND it slips past the project's static anti-leakage audit untouched, because ORACLE_A_CONSEQUENCE_FIELDS only lists the ACHIEVED attitude (ATT.Roll/Pitch); DesRoll/DesPitch are not in that set. So the existing audit does NOT, by itself, rule out a 'demanded attitude' Tier-1 policy. The defense is a firmware-semantics argument, which I verified at source: the GUIDED_NOGPS rate-only path (ModeGuided::angle_control_run -> AC_AttitudeControl::input_rate_bf_roll_pitch_yaw) applies NO aparm.angle_max clamp to the target attitude; the ONLY consumers of aparm.angle_max are get_pilot_desired_lean_angles (RC stick lean conversion), ACRO/FLOWHOLD/FLIP/AUTOROTATE, and the pre-arm leaning check -- never the GUIDED rate path; AC_AttitudeControl.cpp contains no angle_max constraint on the target quaternion/euler state (only a hardcoded +-85 deg pitch clamp in a different euler-rate branch). Therefore ANGLE_MAX is a clamp on PILOT-COMMANDED lean (already faithfully covered by T1a, which sees max commanded 44 deg and does NOT fire), not a contracted bound on the achieved or desired attitude on the rate path. 'Demanded attitude <= ANGLE_MAX' is thus a misreading of a doc string, not an FC contract -- it is a physical safety goal, correctly Tier-2 (essentially T2a). RECOMMENDATION: (1) add ATT.DesRoll and ATT.DesPitch to ORACLE_A_CONSEQUENCE_FIELDS (or add an explicit code-path argument) so the anti-leakage audit mechanically blocks a 'demanded-attitude' Tier-1 policy, closing the one real gap; (2) cite the firmware evidence (input_rate_bf_roll_pitch_yaw has no angle_max clamp) in the paper to justify why ANGLE_MAX is a command clamp, not an attitude contract.

PGFUZZ/RVFUZZER FAITHFULLY SUPPORT C2. I extracted the full PGFUZZ NDSS'21 ArduPilot policy table (A.RTL1-4, A.LAND1-2, A.ALT_HOLD1-2, A.FLIP1-3, A.CIRCLE1-7, A.AUTO1, A.BRAKE1, A.LOITER1, A.GUIDED1, A.SPORT1, A.RC.FS1-2, A.CHUTE1, A.GPS.FS1-2, A.DRIFT1). Every one is a mode-gated behavioral/failsafe invariant; NONE is a universal 'attitude <= ANGLE_MAX' contract. The two numeric roll bounds (A.FLIP1/2, 45 deg) are gated on Mode=FLIP and are vacuously satisfied here (never enters FLIP). The only GUIDED policy, A.GUIDED1 (hold pos/yaw/alt when Waypoint=0), would fire on the altitude collapse but (i) reads POS/altitude = consequence fields => Tier-2 (it is essentially T2b), and (ii) its 'no command' precondition is false while the operator streams rate setpoints. PGFUZZ itself classifies 'unstable attitude' as a PHYSICAL-IMPACT bug category and notes RVFuzzer uses a single stable-attitude/flight-path control-instability detector -- i.e. an OUTCOME oracle = our Tier-2, exactly the seam the paper names.

GENUINE FC CONTRACTS STAY SILENT (which is the point of C2). The two real, firmware-implemented FC contracts I tested that COULD have fired -- the crash_check/thrust_loss_check loss-of-control guard (FS_CRASH_CHECK=1) and the EKF-variance failsafe (FS_EKF_ACTION=LAND, FS_EKF_THRESH=0.8) -- both stay silent in the OverDraw region for documented reasons (crash_check's accel<3 / 2 s persistence never met during the tumble; EKF velocity variance peaks at 1.0 for only ~0.1 s, far below the 1 s persistence and 2-of-3/position-dominant gate). No CRASH_CHECK ERR, no EKFCHECK ERR, no EKF_FAILSAFE/CRASH_FAILSAFE mode reason appear in the trace. These silences strengthen C2: the FC's own documented guards do not consider this trajectory a contract violation until ground impact (a simulator physics event, not a firmware contract). Net: C2 holds; the only action item is hardening the anti-leakage audit against a demanded-attitude policy and stating the ANGLE_MAX-is-a-command-clamp firmware argument explicitly.

omitted_policies.name: C-DESATT: demanded/target attitude (ATT.DesRoll, ATT.DesPitch) must stay <= ANGLE_MAX
omitted_policies.doc_source: ArduCopter/Parameters.cpp:350-357 ANGLE_MAX doc string verbatim: '@Description: Maximum lean angle in all flight modes' (range 1000-8000 cd). A naive PGFUZZ/RVFuzzer checker reading the param docs would lift this into a policy on the logged DESIRED attitude (DesRoll/DesPitch), which it can see in the ATT message. PGFUZZ paper Table (S2 Attitude state) explicitly tracks 'Measured AND desired attitude... reference roll, reference pitch, reference yaw' as monitored state, so a DesRoll-vs-ANGLE_MAX policy is squarely within the PGFUZZ state model.
omitted_policies.empirical_test: On planc/logs/oracleAv1_grid_default_r0180...s01: hypot(DesRoll,DesPitch) max = 176.7 deg vs ANGLE_MAX 45 deg; 319/1697 ATT samples over the limit; sustained > 45 deg for 22.2 s continuous (sustained_exceed dur 0.5s). FIRES hard. CRITICALLY: it reads only ATT.DesRoll/DesPitch + params.ANGLE_MAX, which are DISJOINT from ORACLE_A_CONSEQUENCE_FIELDS (only ATT.Roll/Pitch -- the achieved attitude -- are flagged as consequence), so it PASSES the project's static anti-leakage audit unchanged. This is the single most dangerous omission. HOWEVER it is NOT a faithful contract: firmware grep proves the GUIDED_NOGPS rate-only path (ModeGuided::angle_control_run -> AC_AttitudeControl::input_rate_bf_roll_pitch_yaw) applies NO angle_max clamp to the target attitude; the ONLY consumers of aparm.angle_max are get_pilot_desired_lean_angles (RC stick modes), ACRO, FLOWHOLD, FLIP, AUTOROTATE and the pre-arm leaning check (AP_Arming.cpp:608) -- none on the GUIDED rate path. AC_AttitudeControl.cpp has no aparm.angle_max constraint on _euler_angle_target/_attitude_target (only a hardcoded +-85 deg pitch clamp at line 405 in a different path). So 'demanded attitude <= ANGLE_MAX in all modes' is a misreading of the doc string: the firmware promises ANGLE_MAX only as a clamp on PILOT-COMMANDED lean (which the baseline already covers as T1a, max commanded 44 deg, no violation). The DESIRED attitude on the rate path is an internal integrator state, not a contracted output. Treating DesRoll<=ANGLE_MAX as a contract conflates 'doc string text' with 'firmware FC contract' -- it is a physical-state safety goal (Tier-2), identical in spirit to T2a.

omitted_policies.name: C-ACHATT: achieved attitude (ATT.Roll, ATT.Pitch) must stay <= ANGLE_MAX (the literal 'all flight modes' reading)
omitted_policies.doc_source: Same ANGLE_MAX doc ('maximum lean angle in all flight modes'), but applied to the ACHIEVED roll/pitch. This is the most literal reading of the parameter description and is what an unsophisticated rule-checker would encode.
omitted_policies.empirical_test: max hypot(Roll,Pitch) = 178.2 deg, 247/1697 samples over 45 deg. FIRES. BUT it reads ATT.Roll/ATT.Pitch, which ARE in ORACLE_A_CONSEQUENCE_FIELDS, so it is a textbook consequence/outcome detector -- the anti-leakage audit correctly reclassifies it to Tier-2. It is identical to the existing T2a (achieved attitude bound) which already fires on 507/542 and 59/65 runs. Not a contract: ANGLE_MAX is never enforced as a bound on achieved attitude by any firmware path (it is a setpoint clamp, and even on stick modes the achieved attitude can transiently exceed it). This is a pure physical safety goal.

omitted_policies.name: C-GUIDED1: A.GUIDED1 -- in GUIDED with no waypoint the vehicle must hold position, heading and altitude
omitted_policies.doc_source: PGFUZZ NDSS'21 Table XII, policy A.GUIDED1 (verbatim MTL): {(Mode_t=GUIDED) and (Waypoint=0) -> (Pos_t=Pos_{t-1}) and (Yaw_t=Yaw_{t-1}) and (ALT_t=ALT_{t-1})}. This is the ONLY GUIDED-mode policy in the PGFUZZ ArduPilot set and is directly on-point for the OverDraw scenario (GUIDED/GUIDED_NOGPS).
omitted_policies.empirical_test: Sample trace mode timeline: GUIDED at 8.6s/58.0s then GUIDED_NOGPS at 76.9s. Altitude during window: 42.5 m -> -0.7 m (drop 43.3 m), so position/altitude hold is grossly violated -> A.GUIDED1 FIRES. BUT: (a) it reads POS.RelHomeAlt (and position/yaw), which is in ORACLE_A_CONSEQUENCE_FIELDS -> Tier-2 by the project's own classification; it is functionally a superset of existing T2b (altitude loss). (b) It is also arguably inapplicable as written: the operator is actively STREAMING SET_ATTITUDE_TARGET body-rate setpoints, so 'Waypoint=0 / no command' precondition is false -- the vehicle is being commanded, not idle-holding. PGFUZZ's A.GUIDED1 targets an idle GUIDED hold, not an actively-rate-commanded vehicle. So it is a SOTIF outcome policy (Tier-2), not an FC contract, and does not move C2.

omitted_policies.name: C-ATTSTABLE: PGFUZZ/RVFuzzer 'stable attitude' control-instability policy (sustained attitude-tracking deviation)
omitted_policies.doc_source: RVFuzzer USENIX'19 control-instability detector ('observed/reference state deviation', a single stable-attitude+flight-path policy) and PGFUZZ bug category 3 'unstable attitude (unstable roll, pitch, yaw)'. PGFUZZ paper explicitly: 'RVFuzzer only uses one policy that defines the stable attitude and a correct flight path' and classifies unstable attitude as a PHYSICAL-IMPACT bug category, computing error against the REFERENCE state (e.g. ALTerr=ALTref-ALTact analog for attitude).
omitted_policies.empirical_test: Attitude tracking error hypot(Roll-DesRoll, Pitch-DesPitch) max = 143.8 deg sustained for tens of seconds. FIRES. This is precisely the baseline's existing Tier-2 T2a (sustained achieved-attitude error > 60 deg for >= 0.5 s, which already hits 507/542 + 59/65 runs). RVFuzzer/PGFUZZ themselves classify this as a physical-outcome/control-instability detector, NOT a flight-controller contract -- it is exactly the SOTIF seam the paper is naming. So it is faithfully Tier-2 and confirms rather than threatens C2.

omitted_policies.name: C-CRASHPRED: firmware crash_check / thrust_loss_check predicate (the FC's own documented loss-of-control detector)
omitted_policies.doc_source: ArduCopter/crash_check.cpp:4-7,22-95 (CRASH_CHECK: att_error>30 deg AND lean>15 deg AND speed<10 m/s AND accel<3 m/s/s sustained 2 s -> disarm, Write_Error(CRASH_CHECK)) and crash_check.cpp:100-176 (THRUST_LOSS_CHECK). These ARE genuine firmware-implemented guards with FS_CRASH_CHECK param (=1 in the snapshot).
omitted_policies.empirical_test: Re-implemented the firmware predicate on the sample trace: in-window lean>15 deg for 264/296 samples, att_err>30 deg for 69 samples, speed<10 m/s for ~70% of window -- BUT the trace contains NO CRASH_CHECK ERR and NO CRASH_FAILSAFE mode reason (verified: r.errs has only a benign COMPASS ecode=0; EV stream is ARMED/AUTO_ARMED/SET_HOME/NOT_LANDED only). The firmware crash-check does NOT fire because the 4 conditions (notably accel<3 m/s/s, sustained 2 s) are not simultaneously met during the violent tumble; the firmware only registers ground impact via 'SIM Hit ground' (simulator physics, not a firmware contract). The baseline correctly classifies crash_check as a Tier-2 post-impact consequence detector (CRASH_DETECTOR_SUBSYSTEMS), explicitly excluded from T1b. Since the firmware's own crash contract never actuates in the OverDraw region, including it as a contract policy yields zero Tier-1 hits -- it CONFIRMS C2 (a real FC guard stays silent), it does not threaten it.

omitted_policies.name: C-EKFFS: EKF-failsafe / variance-health contract (FS_EKF_ACTION, XKF4 variances over FS_EKF_THRESH)
omitted_policies.doc_source: ArduCopter/ekf_check.cpp:30-160 (ekf_check + ekf_over_threshold: bad variance for EKF_CHECK_ITERATIONS_MAX=10 iters/1 s, where position_var>=thresh & count>=1 OR count>=2, vel_var>=2x thresh counts double); FS_EKF_THRESH default 0.8 (config.h:128), FS_EKF_ACTION default LAND (config.h:125). FS_EKF_ACTION=1 in the param snapshot.
omitted_policies.empirical_test: This is a GENUINE FC contract (a documented, firmware-implemented failsafe with a configured action), and the baseline's T1c already covers EKFCHECK/FAILSAFE_EKFINAV ACTUATION. Empirically on the sample trace: XKF4 velocity variance SV peaks at 1.0 but only for 2 samples (t=89.8-89.9 s, ~0.1 s, far short of the 1 s persistence requirement); position var SP max 0.13 (< 0.8), height SH 0.16, mag SM 2.26. The ekf_over_threshold gate (pos>=0.8 needed for the dominant term, or 2 simultaneous over-threshold) is never satisfied for the required duration, so NO EKFCHECK ERR / EKF_FAILSAFE appears in the trace (confirmed: r.errs empty of EKF). The raw XKF4.FS bitmask is nonzero (=128) only at t=3.4-4.3 s during pre-arm EKF alignment, not during the maneuver. So the legitimate EKF contract does NOT fire -- T1c is correct to report 0. A checker that instead thresholded the RAW XKF4 variance/FS bitmask (not the documented failsafe actuation) could be made to fire, but that is exactly the leakage trap the baseline names: XKF4.FS is in ORACLE_A_CONSEQUENCE_FIELDS and a raw-variance threshold is a filter-internal health flag correlated with crash dynamics, NOT the documented EKF-failsafe contract. Faithful EKF contract = silent => confirms C2.

omitted_policies.name: C-ARMLEAN: pre-arm / arm-time lean-angle check against ANGLE_MAX
omitted_policies.doc_source: ArduCopter/AP_Arming.cpp:608: if (degrees(acos(cos_roll*cos_pitch))*100 > aparm.angle_max) check_failed(ARMING_CHECK_INS,'Leaning'). A real arming contract enforced by the FC.
omitted_policies.empirical_test: This is a genuine FC contract but is a PRE-ARM/ARM-TIME gate evaluated only at the arming transition, when the vehicle is on the ground and level. Sample trace: 'Arming motors' at t=58.0 s with the vehicle level; the lean excursion to 176 deg happens AFTER arming (during GUIDED_NOGPS at 76.9 s+). The arm-lean check structurally cannot fire on an in-flight excursion. No 'Leaning' prearm message in the trace. So it is silent in the OverDraw region by construction -> confirms C2.

omitted_policies.name: C-FLIP45: PGFUZZ A.FLIP1/A.FLIP2 roll-within-45/[-90,45]-degree policies
omitted_policies.doc_source: PGFUZZ Table XII A.FLIP1 (Roll_t not > 45 as precondition to enter FLIP) and A.FLIP2 ({Mode=FLIP and -90<=Roll<=45 -> Rollrate=400}). These are the only explicit numeric roll-bound policies in the PGFUZZ ArduPilot set.
omitted_policies.empirical_test: Both are GATED on Mode=FLIP. The OverDraw trace never enters FLIP mode (modes are STABILIZE->GUIDED->GUIDED_NOGPS), so the antecedent (Mode_t=FLIP) is never satisfied -> the MTL formula is vacuously true -> does NOT fire. Confirms that PGFUZZ's 45-degree roll references are mode-specific behavioral invariants for FLIP, NOT a universal attitude contract. This directly rebuts the idea that PGFUZZ encodes a general 'attitude <= ANGLE_MAX' contract.

completeness.overall_assessment: The only candidate that fires broadly on the OverDraw region (65/65 runs) is P1: 'vehicle/demanded attitude must stay <= ANGLE_MAX' read as a state-property predicate. This is precisely the policy a real PGFUZZ author would write (PGFUZZ encodes policies as MTL predicates over physical STATES, and the project's own research plan, overdraw_research_plan.md:199, lists '姿态界/attitude bounds' as a policy to reuse). HOWEVER, P1 is NOT a faithful Tier-1 (FuSA) contract -- it is a Tier-2 physical safety goal wearing a contract's clothes, and the baseline correctly classifies it as T2a. Source evidence is decisive: (1) ANGLE_MAX is enforced in firmware ONLY in pilot-stick / euler-angle command paths (get_pilot_desired_lean_angles, the stabilize/althold/auto/loiter modes) and as a one-shot pre-ARM 'Leaning' check (AP_Arming.cpp:608); (2) the GUIDED_NOGPS rate_only path (mode_guided.cpp:964 -> input_rate_bf_roll_pitch_yaw, AC_AttitudeControl.cpp:421-455) integrates body-rate commands into the attitude target with NO lean-angle clamp at all. Therefore the firmware never PROMISES demanded/achieved attitude <= ANGLE_MAX in the rate path; the operator's commands are in-spec and accepted by design. A policy that fires here is detecting an unsafe OUTCOME, not a violated rule -- which is exactly the SOTIF-vs-FuSA seam C2 is about. The distinction the baseline draws (ANGLE_MAX governs COMMANDS, not body-rate setpoints; attitude excursions are T2) is firmware-faithful and survives scrutiny. The genuinely faithful Tier-1 candidates I could construct -- attitude-tracking/reference-following (P2), EKF health (P3), actuator authority (P4), arm-time lean check (P5), GUIDED command-acceptance (P6) -- all FAIL to fire on the sample OverDraw trace, for sound mechanistic reasons: the controller correctly tracks its own (diverging) setpoint (in-window median tracking error 6.7 deg, never sustained >30 deg/2s), the EKF stays healthy (XKF4.FS=0 in-window), motors are not railed (ThrOut<=0.95, FailFlags is a static constant), and the rate commands are accepted by design. NET: C2 survives. The real residual risk is rhetorical/definitional, not empirical: a hostile reviewer can claim a PGFUZZ implementer would naively include the attitude-bound state-predicate (P1) and that the paper's separation of it into Tier-2 is a convenient relabeling. Two recommendations to harden the paper: (i) pre-empt P1 explicitly by citing the firmware source showing ANGLE_MAX has no rate-path enforcement, framing P1 as a SOTIF safety goal a priori; (ii) tighten the anti-leakage audit's consequence set -- ATT.DesRoll/ATT.DesPitch (which reach 176 deg) are NOT currently listed in ORACLE_A_CONSEQUENCE_FIELDS even though they are firmware-computed consequences of executing the rate commands, an inconsistency a reviewer could exploit if any future Tier-1 policy were to read DesRoll/DesPitch.

omitted_policies.name: P1: Vehicle/demanded attitude must remain <= ANGLE_MAX (state-property attitude-bound policy)
omitted_policies.doc_source: This is the central threat. (a) PGFUZZ (Kim et al., USENIX Sec 2021) formulates policies as MTL predicates over PHYSICAL STATES, and its ArduCopter policy set explicitly includes an attitude/roll-pitch bound policy keyed to the configured limit. (b) The project's OWN research plan, planc/docs/overdraw_research_plan.md:199, instructs running a PGFUZZ-style checker reusing its policy set explicitly named as '姿态界' (attitude bounds), mode invariants, failsafe-should-trigger. (c) ArduPilot documents ANGLE_MAX (ArduCopter/Parameters.cpp:350-357) as 'Maximum lean angle in ALL flight modes' -- the word ALL invites reading it as a vehicle-attitude envelope, not merely a command clamp. A naive but DOCUMENTATION-FAITHFUL PGFUZZ author would write predicate: lean_angle(Roll,Pitch) <= ANGLE_MAX, evaluated on the telemetry attitude.
omitted_policies.empirical_test: On the sample trace (ANGLE_MAX=45): achieved lean angle acos(cosRoll*cosPitch) reaches 178.2 deg, demanded (DesRoll/DesPitch) reaches 176.7 deg. sustained_exceed(>45deg,0.5s): achieved fires (max sustained 4.8s), demanded fires (max sustained 22.2s). Swept across the full oracleAv1 set: the demanded-lean>ANGLE_MAX-for-0.5s predicate fires 65/65 and achieved-lean fires 65/65, vs the operator-command clamp T1a firing 0/65.

omitted_policies.name: P2: Attitude-tracking / reference-following contract (achieved attitude must track the firmware's OWN demanded attitude)
omitted_policies.doc_source: RVFuzzer (Kim et al., USENIX Sec 2019) targets control-instability: the controller must keep state near its reference; an unbounded tracking error is a control-level malfunction. ArduPilot's crash_check itself encodes a tracking-error invariant: get_att_error_angle_deg() > 30 deg (CRASH_CHECK_ANGLE_DEVIATION_DEG, ArduCopter/crash_check.cpp:5) is treated as 'out of control'. This is a genuine controller-implementation contract: does the FC achieve what it commands itself?
omitted_policies.empirical_test: On the sample trace, |achieved - DEMANDED| attitude error: max instantaneous 143.8 deg BUT median in-window only 6.7 deg, p95 78.8 deg, and it is NEVER sustained: >30deg for 2s = False (max sustained run 0.6s); >30deg for 1s = False. The controller IS tracking its own setpoint; the SETPOINT itself diverges. This is exactly why a faithful tracking-error contract does NOT fire: the firmware correctly executes the (legal) rate commands. crash_check does not fire for the same reason combined with speed>10m/s and accel>3m/s/s gating.

omitted_policies.name: P3: EKF health / estimator-failsafe contract (XKF4.FS filter-fault bitmask must be clean; FS_EKF_ACTION)
omitted_policies.doc_source: ArduPilot EKF failsafe docs + FS_EKF_THRESH/FS_EKF_ACTION params; XKF4.FS is the documented EKF filter-status/fault bitmask. RVFuzzer/PGFUZZ commonly watch sensor/estimator health. The checker (contract_baseline_v1.py:414-418) deliberately excludes XKF4.FS as a 'leakage trap'.
omitted_policies.empirical_test: XKF4.FS (core 0) = 0 for the entire maneuver window (310 samples, all 0); the value 128 appears only 10x at pre-flight init. errRP (EKF innovation) stays <=0.108 in-window. No EKFCHECK/FAILSAFE_EKFINAV ERR or EKF_FAILSAFE mode reason exists. The EKF stays perfectly healthy through the 176-deg divergence, so an EKF-health contract correctly does NOT fire. Its exclusion does not weaken C2.

omitted_policies.name: P4: Motor saturation / thrust-loss / actuator-authority contract (MOTB.FailFlags clean, ThrOut not railed, thrust_loss_check)
omitted_policies.doc_source: ArduPilot MOTB log (AP_MotorsMulticopter.cpp:436) FailFlags + ThLimit; thrust_loss_check (ArduCopter/crash_check.cpp). PGFUZZ/RVFuzzer-style actuator-saturation policies. A contract tester might assert 'motors not saturated / no thrust loss'.
omitted_policies.empirical_test: MOTB.FailFlags is a constant 2 across the ENTIRE run (1697/1697 rows, including the safe pre-maneuver phase) -- it is a static configuration flag, not a fault that arises during OverDraw, so it cannot discriminate and would be a baseline false-positive if treated as a violation. ThrOut in-window maxes at 0.95 (not pinned at the 1.0 rail). No thrust_loss_check/THRUST_LOSS_CHECK ERR fires. A motor/actuator-authority contract does NOT fire on OverDraw.

omitted_policies.name: P5: Arming-time lean-angle ('Leaning') check (ARMING_CHECK_INS lean<=ANGLE_MAX)
omitted_policies.doc_source: ArduCopter/AP_Arming.cpp:607-611: arm_checks rejects arming if degrees(acos(cosRoll*cosPitch))*100 > angle_max with 'Leaning'. A real PGFUZZ ArduCopter checker that models pre-arm/arm checks would include this.
omitted_policies.empirical_test: This is a pre-ARM gate (function arm_checks), evaluated once before takeoff while the vehicle sits level. The OverDraw vehicle arms level (no 'Leaning' message in the MSG stream; only normal init/EKF/arming texts present) and the divergence occurs in-flight ~70s after arming. The check is structurally incapable of firing in flight. Confirms ANGLE_MAX-vs-attitude is enforced only at arm time, never as an in-flight invariant -- this is firmware-faithful, and does NOT fire on OverDraw.

omitted_policies.name: P6: GUIDED command-acceptance / setpoint-validity contract (rejected/clamped SET_ATTITUDE_TARGET)
omitted_policies.doc_source: ArduPilot GUIDED command handling (ModeGuided::set_angle / angle_control_run, ArduCopter/mode_guided.cpp:909-977). PGFUZZ mutates MAVLink commands and checks whether the FC rejects out-of-spec commands; a command-acceptance contract asserts illegal setpoints are rejected/clamped.
omitted_policies.empirical_test: DECISIVE source evidence: in rate_only mode the attitude_quat is zero, so angle_control_run() (mode_guided.cpp:964) calls input_rate_bf_roll_pitch_yaw(), and AC_AttitudeControl::input_rate_bf_roll_pitch_yaw (AC_AttitudeControl.cpp:421-455) integrates the body-rate command directly into the _attitude_target quaternion with NO ANGLE_MAX / lean-angle limiter. ANGLE_MAX is applied ONLY in the pilot-stick/euler-angle paths (mode_stabilize/althold/drift/flowhold/auto, via get_pilot_desired_lean_angles, mode.cpp:415-432). So the rate command IS within spec and is accepted by design; there is NO documented acceptance contract it violates. Empirically: zero command-rejection / 'tilt' / clamp messages in the trace (only init + 'SIM Hit ground'). A faithful command-acceptance contract correctly does NOT fire.
